rule_gaps: 'teppe' is read as a floor rug everywhere: pledd (throw), sengeteppe (bedspread), ullteppe, laken, påslakensett, putetrekk and pyntepute rows all land on facets.type=Rugs — 18 rows here; the Rugs rule needs the pledd/laken/pute/duk words carved out first

the Jernia/NetOnNet breadcrumbs 'Hjem > Oppbevaring og praktisk hjem > …' and 'Støvsugere og rengjøring > Rengjøringsmidler' are read at the department crumb, so cleaning fluids, tablets, cloths, pipe fittings, extension cords and reflectors get type=Storage / type=Vacuums (12 rows)
srcCat leaf 'Senger med oppbevaring' / 'Oppbevaring' beats the parent 'Møbler > Senger', so whole beds classify as Home storage instead of Furniture
no row in the shard has facets.protocol despite 12 Hue rows whose specs state Zigbee/Bluetooth, and no robot-vacuum row has facets.mop — both declared Home facets are effectively dead
'Pendellampe' (pendant lamp) resolves to Home rather than the Lighting category
bath mats split three ways on type (Rugs / Bath / nothing) depending on the shop
notes: Category assignment is broadly right — the shard is genuinely Home — but facets.type is the weak spot: 30 of 300 rows carry a type contradicted by the name, almost all from two derivation gaps ('teppe'→Rugs and the Norwegian retail 'Oppbevaring/Rengjøring' department crumbs). Everything else is long-tail: 8 demotions (curtain-track fittings, a kr 1 spare lid, two chocolate bars), 5 wrong categories that a shopper would notice (a toy vacuum in Home, a bed, a sun lounger, a silver carving fork, pendant lamps), 30 unwired variant families (mostly JYSK blinds and JYSK/Kid cushion covers) and 4 ALL-CAPS/padded feed names. Icon is 'lamp' on 285 of 300 rows (the Home default) and 143 rows have no image — both shard-wide and not reported per row.
